sections.theory:
Key Points

Carboxylic acids are organic acids having carboxyl group as the functional group (“carb” from carbonyl and “oxyl” from hydroxyl).

Acyl halides, acid anhydrides, esters, amides etc. are the derivatives of carboxylic acids obtained by replacing the –OH of carboxyl group by other functional groups.

Some members of carboxylic acids have penetrating smells. They are water soluble and their solubility decreases with the increase in molecular mass.

Carboxylic acids, due to strong hydrogen bonds, have high boiling points than corresponding alcohols.

The carbon atom of the carboxyl group is sp²-hybridized.

Carboxylic acids are the strongest organic acids, stronger than phenol, alcohols and water.

Substituents in a carboxylic acid molecules strongly influence the strength of the acid due to the inductive effect of the substituent.

Carboxylic acids can be prepared from Grignard reagent by oxidation of alcohols and aldehydes and by hydrolysis of nitriles.

Although the carboxylic group contains the carbonyl group, yet carboxylic acid do not exhibit some of the characteristic reactions of aldehydes and ketones.

Carboxylic acids, on reaction with different species, can be converted to their derivatives.

Among the derivatives of carboxylic acids, acyl halides are the most reactive.

All of the acid derivatives can be converted back into the corresponding carboxylic acids on hydrolysis.

Key Points

Carboxylic acids are organic acids having carboxyl group as the functional group (“carb” from carbonyl and “oxyl” from hydroxyl).

Acyl halides, acid anhydrides, esters, amides etc. are the derivatives of carboxylic acids obtained by replacing the –OH of carboxyl group by other functional groups.

Some members of carboxylic acids have penetrating smells. They are water soluble and their solubility decreases with the increase in molecular mass.

Carboxylic acids, due to strong hydrogen bonds, have high boiling points than corresponding alcohols.

The carbon atom of the carboxyl group is sp²-hybridized.

Carboxylic acids are the strongest organic acids, stronger than phenol, alcohols and water.

Substituents in a carboxylic acid molecules strongly influence the strength of the acid due to the inductive effect of the substituent.

Carboxylic acids can be prepared from Grignard reagent by oxidation of alcohols and aldehydes and by hydrolysis of nitriles.

Although the carboxylic group contains the carbonyl group, yet carboxylic acid do not exhibit some of the characteristic reactions of aldehydes and ketones.

Carboxylic acids, on reaction with different species, can be converted to their derivatives.

Among the derivatives of carboxylic acids, acyl halides are the most reactive.

All of the acid derivatives can be converted back into the corresponding carboxylic acids on hydrolysis.

sections.theory:
Exercise

Q 1. Choose the correct one from the given options.

1. Which of the following represents the formula of an aromatic carboxylic acids?

a. HCOOH   b. C₆H₅OH   c. C₆H₅COOH   d. C₆H₅CH₂OH

2. Which of the following acids is found in rancid butter?

a. C₂H₄O₂   b. C₃H₆O₂   c. C₄H₈O₂   d. C₅H₁₀O₂

3. The compound with highest boiling point is

a. acetic acid.   b. water.   c. ethyl alcohol.   d. diethyl ether.

4. In which of the following compounds, the carbon atom does not show sp²-hybridization?

a. Methanal   b. Methanol   c. Methanoic acid   d. Acetone

5. Which is the strongest acid?

a. Ethanol   b. Acetic acid   c. Chloroacetic acid   d. Fluoroacetic acid

6. Acetic acid can be prepared by the hydrolysis of

a. methyl cyanide.   b. methylmagnescium chloride.   c. ethanal.   d. ethanol.

7. Fischer esterification is the reaction between

a. an acid and ester.   b. an acid and alcohol.   c. an acid halide and ester.   d. an ester and sodium hydroxide.

8. Acyl chloride can be prepared by the reaction of a carboxylic acid with

a. phosphorous pentoxide.   b. soda lime.   c. hydrochloric acid.   d. thionyl chloride.

9. The hydrolysis of an ester in presence of alkali is known as

a. saponification.   b. decarboxylation.   c. esterification.   d. transesterfication.

10. All the acid derivatives can be converted back into the corresponding acid by one common reaction.

a. ammonolysis   b. alcoholysis   c. reduction   d. hydrolysis

مشق

سوال 1. دیے گئے اختیارات میں سے درست کا انتخاب کریں۔

1. درج ذیل میں سے کون سا ارومیٹک کاربوکسلک ایسڈ کا فارمولا ظاہر کرتا ہے؟

a. HCOOH   b. C₆H₅OH   c. C₆H₅COOH   d. C₆H₅CH₂OH

2. درج ذیل میں سے کون سا ایسڈ باسی مکھن میں پایا جاتا ہے؟

a. C₂H₄O₂   b. C₃H₆O₂   c. C₄H₈O₂   d. C₅H₁₀O₂

3. سب سے زیادہ نقطۂ جوش والا مرکب ہے

a. ایسیٹک ایسڈ۔   b. پانی۔   c. ایتھائل الکوحل۔   d. ڈائی ایتھائل ایتھر۔

4. درج ذیل میں سے کس مرکب میں کاربن ایٹم sp²-ہائبرڈائزیشن ظاہر نہیں کرتا؟

a. میتھانل   b. میتھانول   c. میتھانوئک ایسڈ   d. ایسیٹون

5. سب سے طاقتور ایسڈ کون سا ہے؟

a. ایتھانول   b. ایسیٹک ایسڈ   c. کلورو ایسیٹک ایسڈ   d. فلورو ایسیٹک ایسڈ

6. ایسیٹک ایسڈ کس کی ہائیڈرولائسز سے تیار کیا جا سکتا ہے

a. میتھائل سائنائیڈ۔   b. میتھائل میگنیشیم کلورائیڈ۔   c. ایتھانل۔   d. ایتھانول۔

7. فشر ایسٹریفکیشن کس کے درمیان تعامل ہے

a. ایسڈ اور ایسٹر۔   b. ایسڈ اور الکوحل۔   c. ایسڈ ہیلائیڈ اور ایسٹر۔   d. ایسٹر اور سوڈیم ہائیڈروآکسائیڈ۔

8. ایسائل کلورائیڈ کاربوکسلک ایسڈ کے کس سے تعامل سے تیار کیا جا سکتا ہے

a. فاسفورس پینٹا آکسائیڈ۔   b. سوڈا لائم۔   c. ہائیڈروکلورک ایسڈ۔   d. تھایونائل کلورائیڈ۔

9. القلی کی موجودگی میں ایسٹر کی ہائیڈرولائسز کہلاتی ہے

a. سیپونیفکیشن۔   b. ڈی کاربوکسیلیشن۔   c. ایسٹریفکیشن۔   d. ٹرانس ایسٹریفکیشن۔

10. تمام ایسڈ مشتقات ایک مشترک تعامل سے واپس متعلقہ ایسڈ میں تبدیل کیے جا سکتے ہیں۔

a. امونولائسز   b. الکوحلائسز   c. تخفیف   d. ہائیڈرولائسز

a. فاسفورس پنټا اکساید.   b. سوډا لایم.   c. هایدروکلوریک اسید.   d. تایونیل کلوراید.

9. د قلوي په شتون کې د ایسټر هایدرولایسس بلل کېږي

a. د صابون جوړونه (سپونیفیکېشن).   b. ډی کاربوکسیلېشن.   c. ایسټریفیکېشن.   d. ټرانس ایسټریفیکېشن.

10. ټول اسید مشتقات د یوه ګډ تعامل په واسطه بېرته اړوند اسید ته بدلېدای شي.

a. امونولایسس   b. الکولایسس   c. ارجاع   d. هایدرولایسس

Exercise

Q 1. Choose the correct one from the given options.

1. Which of the following represents the formula of an aromatic carboxylic acids?

a. HCOOH b. C₆H₅OH c. C₆H₅COOH d. C₆H₅CH₂OH

2. Which of the following acids is found in rancid butter?

a. C₂H₄O₂ b. C₃H₆O₂ c. C₄H₈O₂ d. C₅H₁₀O₂

3. The compound with highest boiling point is

a. acetic acid. b. water. c. ethyl alcohol. d. diethyl ether.

4. In which of the following compounds, the carbon atom does not show sp²-hybridization?

a. Methanal b. Methanol c. Methanoic acid d. Acetone

5. Which is the strongest acid?

a. Ethanol b. Acetic acid c. Chloroacetic acid d. Fluoroacetic acid

6. Acetic acid can be prepared by the hydrolysis of

a. methyl cyanide. b. methylmagnescium chloride. c. ethanal. d. ethanol.

7. Fischer esterification is the reaction between

a. an acid and ester. b. an acid and alcohol. c. an acid halide and ester. d. an ester and sodium hydroxide.

8. Acyl chloride can be prepared by the reaction of a carboxylic acid with

a. phosphorous pentoxide. b. soda lime. c. hydrochloric acid. d. thionyl chloride.

9. The hydrolysis of an ester in presence of alkali is known as

a. saponification. b. decarboxylation. c. esterification. d. transesterfication.

10. All the acid derivatives can be converted back into the corresponding acid by one common reaction.

a. ammonolysis b. alcoholysis c. reduction d. hydrolysis
